newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard cuts business notebook prices 13 percent.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard cuts business notebook prices 13 percent.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. Monday cut list prices by up to 13 percent on its small-business and commercial HP Vectra PC and HP OmniBook notebook PC lines in the United States and Canada.
HP said it cut prices by up to 10 percent on its OmniBook 5700 and 800 notebook PCs as part of the company's aggressive push to reduce computing costs for businesses.

The list price of theOmniBook 5700 CTX is now $5,750, but it is expected to sell for about $5,175 in stores, the company said. HP said that price is 17 percent below a comparably equipped Compaq Armada 7750 PC.
The Palo Alto, Calif., company also cut the list price of a commercial HP Vectra VL PC by 13 percent to $2,059. It is expected to sell for about $1,845.
The list price of an HP Vectra 525 MCx 5/166M designed for small businesses is almost 11 percent lower at $2,009. It is expected to sell for about $1,826.
HP's stock rose 37.5 cents to $52.75 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
